content: 1. A randomized controlled trial conducted in The Gambia was published in The Lancet in 2009, focusing on the efficacy of a house-based intervention influenced by human and mosquito behavior. 2. Barreaux AMG and colleagues explored the role of human and mosquito behavior in the success of house-based interventions in a study published in the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, Series B, Biological Sciences in 2021. 3. The World Health Organization (WHO) released a comprehensive approach to global surveillance, prevention, and control of chronic respiratory diseases in 2007. 4. WHO also published guidelines in 2021 on exposure to household air pollution and in 2014 on indoor air quality related to household fuel combustion. 5. Sundell J and colleagues conducted a multidisciplinary review of scientific literature on ventilation rates and health, published in Indoor Air in 2011. 6. Knudsen JB and colleagues measured ventilation in various rural Gambian house types in a pilot experimental study published in Malaria Journal in 2020. 7. Jatta E and colleagues investigated how house design affects malaria mosquito density, temperature, and relative humidity in rural Gambia, with findings published in The Lancet Planetary Health in 2018. 8. WHO outlined norms, standards, and processes for developing vector control recommendations in 2020. 9. Sicuri E and colleagues evaluated the cost-effectiveness of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria during pregnancy in southern Mozambique, published in PLoS One in 2010. 10. Fernandes S and colleagues modeled the cost-effectiveness of two versus three or more doses of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria during pregnancy in sub-Saharan Africa, published in The Lancet Global Health in 2015. 11. Hansen KS and colleagues analyzed the cost-effectiveness of three health interventions to prevent malaria during pregnancy in low-transmission areas of Uganda, published in International Health in 2012. 12. Diengou NH and colleagues identified factors associated with the uptake of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria during pregnancy in Cameroon, published in The Pan African Medical Journal in 2020. 13. Nekaka R and colleagues studied malaria preventive practices and delivery outcomes among parturient women in a tertiary hospital in Eastern Uganda, published in PLoS One in 2020. 14. Ngapanya S and colleagues conducted a descriptive cross-sectional study on the uptake of intermittent preventive therapy among pregnant women in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, published in SN Comprehensive Clinical Medicine in 2020. 15. Onyebuchi AK and colleagues assessed adherence to WHO guidelines for intermittent preventive treatment of malaria during pregnancy in Southeast Nigeria, published in Patient Preference and Adherence in 2014. 16. Moberg J and colleagues developed the GRADE Evidence to Decision framework for health system and public health decisions, published in Health Research Policy and Systems in 2018. 17. WHO published a policy brief in 2014 for implementing intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy using sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP). 18. WHO released recommendations in 2016 on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience. 19. Esu EB and colleagues reviewed intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in infants, published in The Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2021. 20. Kobbe R and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial on extended intermittent preventive antimalarial treatment in infants, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2007. 21. Mockenhaupt FP and colleagues evaluated intermittent preventive treatment in infants as a malaria control strategy in northern Ghana, published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy in 2007. 22. Grobusch MP and colleagues conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial on intermittent preventive treatment against malaria in infants in Gabon, published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2007. 23. Bigira V and colleagues assessed the protective efficacy and safety of three antimalarial regimens for malaria prevention in young Ugandan children, published in PLoS Medicine in 2014. 24. Griffin JT and colleagues analyzed the protective efficacy of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in infants using sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and parasite resistance, published in PLoS One in 2010. 25. Lahue R and colleagues evaluated health system readiness and coverage of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in infants in Sierra Leone, published in Malaria Journal in 2021. 26. Manzi F and colleagues developed and implemented a public health strategy for malaria and anemia control in Tanzanian infants, published in Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2009. 27. Shea BJ and colleagues introduced AMSTAR 2, a critical appraisal tool for systematic reviews of healthcare interventions, published in BMJ in 2017. 28. WHO published a field guide in 2011 for implementing intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in infants using sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP-IPTi). 29. Paton RS and colleagues studied malaria infection and severe disease risks in Africa, published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2021. 30. Issiaka D and colleagues determined the optimal mode for delivering seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Mali, published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2015. 31. Barry A and colleagues conducted a cluster randomized trial on seasonal malaria chemoprevention delivery in Mali, published in PLoS One in 2018. 32. Ceesay S and colleagues implemented seasonal malaria chemoprevention in The Gambia, published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2016. 33. WHO published a field guide in 2023 for seasonal malaria chemoprevention with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine in children. 34. Clarke SE and colleagues evaluated the effect of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria on health and education in schoolchildren, published in The Lancet in 2008. 35. Nankabirwa J and colleagues assessed the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of three regimens for malaria prevention in Ugandan schoolchildren, published in PLoS One in 2010. 36. Matangila JR and colleagues evaluated the efficacy and safety of intermittent preventive treatment in schoolchildren in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, published in the International Journal of Antimicrobial Agents in 2017. 37. Cohee LM and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on preventive malaria treatment among school-aged children in sub-Saharan Africa, published in The Lancet Global Health in 2020. 38. Audibert C and Tchouatieu A-M studied perceptions of malaria chemoprevention interventions in infants and children in eight sub-Saharan African countries, published in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Disease in 2021. 39. Maccario R and colleagues analyzed the cost of a school-based comprehensive malaria program in Mali, published in BMC Public Health in 2017. 40. Temperley M and colleagues evaluated the costs and cost-effectiveness of delivering intermittent preventive treatment through schools in western Kenya, published in Malaria Journal in 2008. 41. Maiga H and colleagues assessed the effects of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria with artemisinin-based combination therapies among schoolchildren in Mali, published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine & Hygiene in 2022. 42. Rohner F and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial on iron fortification, anthelmintic treatment, and intermittent preventive treatment of malaria for anemia control in Ivorian children, published in The Journal of Nutrition in 2010. 43. Cohee LM and colleagues piloted the addition of mass treatment for malaria to existing school-based programs for neglected tropical diseases, published in The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2018. 44. Staedke SG and colleagues assessed community-level effects of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in schoolchildren in Uganda, published in The Lancet Global Health in 2018. 45. WHO published guidelines in 2011 on hemoglobin concentrations for diagnosing anemia and assessing severity. 46. Phiri K and colleagues evaluated intermittent preventive therapy for malaria with monthly artemether-lumefantrine for post-discharge management of severe anemia in children in Malawi, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2012. 47. Kwambai TK and colleagues studied malaria chemoprevention in the post-discharge management of severe anemia, published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2020. 48. Bojang KA and colleagues investigated the prevention of anemia recurrence in Gambian children following hospital discharge, published in PLoS One in 2010. 49. Nkosi-Gondwe T and colleagues explored community health workers' perceptions and motivations regarding post-discharge malaria chemoprevention in Malawian children, published in BMC Health Services Research in 2018. 50. Nadia J and Lu F reviewed historical experiences with mass drug administration for malaria control and elimination, published in Acta Tropica in 2022. 51. WHO published a practical field manual in 2017 for mass drug administration for falciparum malaria. 52. WHO released the Immunization Agenda 2030, a global strategy to leave no one behind, in 2020. 53. The efficacy and safety of the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine with or without a booster dose in African infants and children were published in The Lancet in 2015. 54. The European Medicines Agency provided an opinion on the use of Mosquirix outside the EU in 2015. 55. Chandramohan D and colleagues studied seasonal malaria vaccination with or without seasonal malaria chemoprevention, published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2021. 56. Datoo MS and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of a low-dose candidate malaria vaccine, R21 in adjuvant Matrix-M, with seasonal administration to children in Burkina Faso, published in The Lancet in 2021.
